assumptions_invoked: €100 arrangement fee paid at t=0 is treated as a charge at t=0, reducing the net amount made available to the consumer: net drawdown = €10,000 - €100 = €9,900 at t=0
24 equal monthly repayments of €450 commence one month after drawdown: times t = k/12 years for k = 1..24
Periods expressed in years; one month = 1/12 year (Annex I remark (c), 30.41666 days/month, so 1 month = 1/12 exactly)
Result rounded to one decimal place per Annex I remark (d) (round half up)
Annex I Part II assumption (d): for overdrafts the total amount is deemed to be drawn in full for the whole duration of the contract
Duration not determinable => assumed 3 months (directive's fallback of 3 months / one quarter = 0.25 years) per Annex I Part II assumption (c)
12% nominal per annum charged monthly => monthly rate = 12%/12 = 1%; interest on €3,000 for 3 months = €3,000*((1.01)^3 - 1) = €90.90
€25 monthly account fee for 3 months = €75.00; total repaid at 3 months = €3,000 + €90.90 + €75.00 = €3,165.90
All charges (interest + fees) paid as a single repayment at t = 3/12 years; one month = 1/12 year; result to one decimal place
Annex I Part II assumption (a): where the consumer has freedom of drawdown (open-end credit), the total credit is deemed to be drawn immediately and in full => €1,500 at t=0
Repayment in 12 equal monthly instalments (source-logic: assumption of equal amortisation over the assumed 12-month horizon, one month = 1/12 year)
18% nominal per annum, monthly compounding => monthly rate i = 0.18/12 = 1.5%; payment p = 1500 / sum_{k=1..12}(1.015)^(-k) = €137.52
No other fees; result to one decimal place
Unascertainable drawdown => Annex I Part II assumption (a): total credit deemed drawn immediately and in full at t=0, so €5,000 drawn at t=0
€200 broker fee financed into the balance at t=0 => added to the amount drawn/borrowed, giving drawdown = €5,000 + €200 = €5,200 at t=0 (this is why it differs from a t=0 cash fee: see below)
Single repayment at 12 months; 8% nominal per annum => repayment = €5,200 * 1.08 = €5,616 at t = 1 year
One month = 1/12 year; result to one decimal place
financed_fee_note: A t=0 cash fee reduces the net amount made available to the consumer (net drawdown = principal - fee), leaving the repayment stream unchanged - it raises the APRC because the consumer receives less up front. A fee financed into the balance instead increases the drawn amount (drawdown rises from €5,000 to €5,200) while the repayment is calculated on that larger balance; here the repayment is 8% of €5,200, so the APRC remains exactly 8% - the fee is silently amortised into the loan rather than paid out of pocket.

weakest_point: Case 2 is the most assumption-heavy and therefore most likely to diverge from the directive's exact method: the treatment of the €25 monthly fee and monthly interest (single lump repayment at 3 months vs. deducted/charged each month), the 3-month duration fallback, and whether the fee reduces the net drawdown or is a separate charge all affect the PV equation. Case 1's treatment of the arrangement fee as a t=0 charge (reducing net drawdown to €9,900 rather than a separate outflow) is the next-most-likely divergence point. The monthly-to-year conversion uses exactly 1/12 throughout, consistent with the Annex convention.
